title: dispatch starts a worker's claude -p with no --settings, so its plugins' MCP servers run unless the orchestrator's PATH wrapper turns them off
goal: backlog.json takes a setting worker_plugins_off (a list of plugin keys, default none) and claude_argv adds --settings with enabledPlugins false for each, so dispatch, begin and dispatch --resume start a worker with those plugins off and no wrapper is needed; this clone's backlog.json lists gitkraken@synced in worker_plugins_off

run:
import glob, json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    bindir = os.path.join(d, "bin"); os.mkdir(bindir)
    log = os.path.join(d, "argv.log")
    open(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), "w").write("#!/bin/sh\necho \"$@\" >> \"$ARGV_LOG\"\ncat >/dev/null\necho '{\"is_error\":false,\"session_id\":\"s\"}'\n")
    os.chmod(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), 0o755)
    env = dict(os.environ, PATH=bindir + os.pathsep + os.environ["PATH"], ARGV_LOG=log, KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(d, "coord.sqlite"))
    origin = os.path.join(d, "origin.git")
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", origin], check=True)
    root = os.path.join(d, "root"); os.mkdir(root)
    def g(*a):
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, *a], capture_output=True, text=True)
    def bl(*a):
        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", "--root", root, *a], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=120)
    g("init", "-q", "-b", "main"); g("config", "user.email", "x@example.com"); g("config", "user.name", "x"); g("remote", "add", "origin", origin)
    json.dump({"worker_plugins_off": ["gitkraken@synced"]}, open(os.path.join(root, "backlog.json"), "w"))
    open(os.path.join(root, "README"), "w").write("x\n"); g("add", "."); g("commit", "-qm", "init"); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main")
    iid = bl("new", "story", "--title", "T", "--goal", "g", "--touch", "f.txt", "--check", "python3 -c pass").stdout.split()[2]
    path = glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", iid + ".json"), recursive=True)[0]
    item = json.load(open(path)); item["status"] = "todo"; json.dump(item, open(path, "w"))
    g("add", "."); g("commit", "-qm", "plant todo"); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main")
    claimed = bl("claim", iid, "--by", "claude-aaaaaaaa")
    assert claimed.returncode == 0, ("claim", (claimed.stdout + claimed.stderr)[-300:])
    dispatched = bl("dispatch", iid)
    argv = open(log).read() if os.path.exists(log) else ""
    assert argv, ("the worker session did not start", (dispatched.stdout + dispatched.stderr)[-300:])
    assert "--settings" in argv and "gitkraken@synced" in argv, ("dispatch gave the worker session no --settings turning the plugin off", argv[:200])
import json,sys; v=json.load(open('backlog.json')).get('worker_plugins_off', []); print('worker_plugins_off:', v); sys.exit(0 if 'gitkraken@synced' in v else 1)

clauses.clause: this clone's backlog.json lists gitkraken@synced in worker_plugins_off

backlog.json takes a setting worker_plugins_off (a list of plugin keys, default none) and claude_argv adds --settings with enabledPlugins false for each, so dispatch, begin and dispatch --resume start a worker with those plugins off and no wrapper is needed

notes: Retro finding of the drain: headless workers must run with the gitkraken plugin off (its gk mcp children orphan in the worker's worktree and block land at step branch); the orchestrator did it with a wrapper named claude first on PATH, kept in a temporary directory that vanished between sessions, so one worker started without it. Premise (reproduces: the repro): claude_argv (bl_dispatch.py) builds the argv with no --settings. The key a plugin takes in enabledPlugins is gitkraken@synced on this host; a committed backlog.json setting is chosen over an environment variable like KB_WORKER_BUDGET_USD because the wrapper failed as a missing out-of-repo file; the setting's default is none, so a host project is unchanged. claude_argv serves new, resumed and begun dispatches, and agent_bench.py and kb_ask.py call it too: keep its signature compatible. The repro plants a root whose backlog.json names the setting and a fake claude that logs its argv.
